ingredientSections.heading: Fish
items: 500g Sablefish fillet cut into 4 portions (sablefish is also known as black cod or coalfish)

methodSections.heading: Marinade
steps: Sauté the coarsely chopped ginger and lemongrass for 5-10 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with the Sake and combine the rest of the ingredients. Simmer until the sugar has dissolved.
Taste to ensure there is a nice balance of salt from the soy sauce and the sweetness from the sugar. Adjust if necessary.
Allow to cool. Add the fillets to the marinade and refrigerate for 6-8 hours.

methodSections.heading: Cooking the Fish
steps: When you are ready to cook the fish, preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F). Sear the sable in a hot oiled fry pan, flesh side down for 15-25 seconds, or until the flesh is slightly crisp but not burnt.
Transfer to an oven-safe dish and bake at 230°C (450°F) for 3-5 minutes.
Garnish with pickled ginger or fish roe (optional).

methodSections.heading: Shrimp Wontons
steps: Chop the prawns finely and season with salt and pepper. Sauté the prawns with a small amount of butter and let cool.
Beat the egg and separate the wonton wraps individually. Lightly moisten the circumference with the egg.
Place even amounts of shrimp in the middle of each wonton and pinch closed.
Rotate the wonton with pinches until the shrimp is sealed. Ensure there is little air left in the wonton. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Steam the wontons in a bamboo steamer for 5 minutes. Start to steam the wontons when the fish goes in the oven.

methodSections.heading: Ponzu Aioli
steps: Combine the soya sauce, fish sauce, lime and lemon juice, adjusting the quantities if necessary to balance the saltiness and acidity.

Blend in the mayonnaise to the point of stability (meaning it won't run on a plate). Refrigerate until ready to use. Use around a tablespoon per serving either drizzle over the fish or use it to help decorate the plate.
